title: entitopia index-config
description: Per-dataset load settings. Every key here is read by entitopia itself, so unknown keys are rejected: a typo that is merely ignored lets a setting fall back to its default with nothing reported, which is this repository's recurring failure shape.

alias.description: Stable read name. Reads through an alias naming more than one index return each document once per attached index, which is silent rather than an error.

index.description: Concrete index name, usually carrying a {now/d} stamp so a reload lands in a fresh index rather than overwriting the same day's run.

source.description: CSV filename, resolved under the project's data directory. Absent for an index a phase WRITES rather than loads — the chameleon-candidates and chameleon-validation indexes have no source file. That is why `source` is not unconditionally required: instead, any key that only means something while loading (id_field, num_rows, skip_rows, pipeline) requires it, so a real dataset config cannot omit it while an output index can.

id_field.description: Natural key. A list composes a deterministic composite id. Absent means Elasticsearch generates one, which duplicates every row on rerun.

num_rows.description: Row cap. null loads everything. A committed non-null value is the validation-sample-left-on-in-production hazard: a 'full' load silently truncates.

skip_rows.description: Leading rows to skip past the header.

pipeline.description: Ingest pipeline to route documents through on load.
